what_it_does: Near-memory processing (NMP) — placing small compute units directly on or inside memory modules so data does not have to travel far — is appealing for memory-hungry AI workloads, but coordinating the NMP unit and the main CPU is tricky. Both sides share the same memory bus (the electrical pathway data travels on), and if they try to use it simultaneously, requests collide and can even corrupt data in the memory chips. Because of this, existing designs force the CPU to pause and wait while the NMP unit works, wasting CPU compute time. AsyncDIMM introduces three operating modes on that shared bus — CPU-only, NMP-only, and a concurrent mode — along with a handoff protocol that lets the CPU keep doing useful work in parallel with the NMP unit while carefully coordinating who accesses the bus and when. Extra engineering work on access timing and batching minimizes the cost of switching between modes. The prototype is built on an FPGA (a reprogrammable chip used for hardware prototyping).
